title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named JMU spaces for studying, quiet time, games, projects, and low-key connection, documented on current university and library pages.

cards.title: Settle into Taylor Down Under
cards.subtitle: The Union · lower level of Taylor Hall
cards.notes: Bring a study partner or take a break: use the couches, tables, pool tables, computer workstations, wireless access, and printing.
cards.short_summary: A flexible Union lounge for homework, downtime, and student-organized events.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU says TDU is open for students to relax, do homework, or pass through, and lists couches, pool tables, computer workstations, wireless access, and printing.
cards.access_notes: Located in the lower level of Taylor Hall; check Union information for current access and event reservations.

cards.title: Work beside the Airport Lounge gallery
cards.subtitle: The Union · Warren Hall, fourth floor
cards.notes: Head to Warren’s fourth floor when you want a quiet place to read, work, or study with curated gallery art nearby.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor Union study lounge with campus views and rotating art.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU identifies Airport Lounge as a quiet space where students can relax, work, or study; it contains gallery photographs and is on The Union’s fourth floor.
cards.access_notes: Located on the fourth floor of Warren Hall in The Union; availability can vary.

cards.title: Take a reset in The Living Room
cards.subtitle: The Union · Warren 420
cards.notes: Use the tea, blankets, pillows, puzzles, games, and seating for a quiet reset, reading session, or low-key conversation.
cards.short_summary: A Counseling Center-designed room for calming down or doing quiet work.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU describes The Living Room in Warren 420 as a serene, neurodivergent-friendly space with tea, blankets, pillows, puzzles, and games.
cards.access_notes: Located in Warren 420; space availability may vary during the year.

cards.title: Pause at the Serenity Center
cards.subtitle: The Union · Warren 419
cards.notes: Use the room for quiet reading, restorative movement, mindfulness, spiritual devotion, or a few minutes of self-regulation.
cards.short_summary: A Union room designed for mindful, restorative activities.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU says the Serenity Center supports relaxation, self-regulation, mindfulness practices, spiritual devotion, restorative movement, and reading.
cards.access_notes: Located in Warren 419; space availability may vary during the year.

cards.title: Find quiet in the Interfaith Space
cards.subtitle: The Union · Taylor 516
cards.notes: Stop in for meditation, prayer, quiet reflection, or group worship; the space welcomes people regardless of denomination or faith.
cards.short_summary: A Union reflection room open to students, faculty, staff, and visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU states that its Interfaith Space welcomes all denominations and faiths for meditation, prayer, quiet time, and group worship.
cards.access_notes: Located in Taylor 516; observe the intended reflective and worship uses.

cards.title: Use Rose’s swipe-in 24-hour space
cards.subtitle: Rose Library · first floor side entrance
cards.notes: Swipe in with your JACard for big tables, group rooms, a computer and printing lab, individual bathrooms, and vending machines.
cards.short_summary: An always-available Rose Library work zone with study and printing amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU Libraries says Rose Library’s 24-Hour Space is available at any hour by swiping into the side door and includes tables, group rooms, computers, printing, bathrooms, and vending.
cards.access_notes: JACard swipe access is required through the Rose Library side door closest to Phys/Chem.

cards.entity_name: Rose Library Hangout Space with Puzzles and Games
cards.title: Break up homework at Rose’s hangout space
cards.subtitle: Rose Library · second floor
cards.notes: Take a short study break with the magazines, games, and LEGO bricks, then return to your work without leaving the library.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor Rose Library break space with games, magazines, and LEGO bricks.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU Libraries lists a second-floor Rose Library Hangout Space with magazines, games, and LEGO bricks.
cards.access_notes: Located on Rose Library’s second floor.

cards.title: Rearrange the Rose flex space
cards.subtitle: Rose Library · third floor
cards.notes: Meet with classmates or spread out solo; mobile chairs, tables, and whiteboards let the setup change with your work.
cards.short_summary: A reconfigurable third-floor study area for solo work or collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU Libraries says Rose Library’s Flex Space has completely mobile chairs, tables, and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Located on Rose Library’s third floor.

cards.title: Focus in Rose’s quiet booths
cards.subtitle: Rose Library · third and fourth floors
cards.notes: Use a booth when you need concentrated individual work: the sound-dampening walls, airflow, adjustable desks, and outlets support it.
cards.short_summary: Individual, sound-dampened Rose Library booths for focused work.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU Libraries describes its Rose Library quiet booths as having individual airflow, sound-dampening walls, and adjustable desks, with booths on the third and fourth floors.
cards.access_notes: First-come availability; booths are on Rose Library’s third and fourth floors.

cards.title: Pair up in The Nook
cards.subtitle: Rose Library · third floor
cards.notes: Walk right from the third-floor elevator and use the big tables, campus views, and whiteboards for partner work or solo homework.
cards.short_summary: A tucked-away Rose Library table area for quiet partner or individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU Libraries says The Nook is on Rose Library’s third floor and offers campus views, big tables, and usually whiteboards for partner or solo work.
cards.access_notes: From the third-floor elevator, turn right and continue to The Nook.
